newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht down late, interbank rate firmer.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht down late, interbank rate firmer.

text.p: The Thai baht was down against the dollar in late trade on Friday on the U.S. unit's uptrend abroad, dealers said.
The baht was traded at 25.970/25.975 to the dollar late compared with 25.965/25.970 in early morning, dealers said.
"The trade was active today with continued buying of the dollar. The expected rise in U.S. interest rates supported the dollar," one dealer at a foreign bank said.
The dollar buying was also triggered by some demand ahead of the month-end and high liquidity in the system, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 25.97 per dollar against 25.94 on Thursday.
The overnight interbank rate firmed to 7.00-8.00 percent late from 6.50-7.00 earlier as banks began to borrow funds on a belief that the interbank rate had bottomed out, dealers said.

"The interbank rate rise has nothing to do with the central bank's increased amount of bond auction today. Most players just believed the interbank rate reached the bottom and will rebound next week," said one money market dealer.
The Bank of Thailand raised its 28-day bill auction to 20 billion baht from 2.0 billion originally planned on Friday. The average yield was 10.38 percent for the bills.

The central bank said it had substantially raised the amount of bonds auctioned to mop up excess liquidity in the system after a scheduled withdrawal of about 70-80 billion baht of start-up funds by the Government Pension Fund on March 27.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 7.80/8.80 satangs per dollar late against 8.00/9.00 in early trade, dealers said.
